slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Moving mailboxes is the easy bit. Almost every migration that goes badly goes badly for the same handful of reasons, and none of them are the mail.

slots.label: List item 1
slots.default: Shared mailboxes, distribution lists and meeting rooms

slots.label: List item 2
slots.default: Folder permissions and who really needs what

slots.label: List item 3
slots.default: Applications signing in with the old accounts

slots.label: List item 4
slots.default: Mobile devices with mail on them

slots.label: List item 5
slots.default: Mailbox and file sizes against your new licences

slots.label: List item 6
slots.default: Old subscriptions to cancel after go live

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Shared mailboxes, distribution lists and meeting rooms get forgotten because no single person owns them, then reappear the morning after cutover when nobody can book anything.

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Permissions on shared folders are assumed to carry over neatly and rarely do, so somebody either loses access to a folder they need or quietly gains access to one they should not have. Third party applications that authenticate against the old system stop working until each one is reconnected, and the list of them is always longer than anyone expects.

slots.label: Heading 4
slots.default: Phones, and the licences still billing

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: Everyone remembers the laptops. Half the workforce has mail on a phone that nobody has recorded anywhere, and if that is not handled they spend cutover morning locked out and irritated. Old licences are the last one, still quietly billing months later because nobody cancelled them.

slots.label: Paragraph 6
slots.default: It just has to be written down beforehand and worked through, which is precisely what the discovery stage is for.
